mappings.note: Asks which WORD the poem uses for the Indian Ocean (sindhu) - a paryayavachi-style lexical item, so C-HIN2.2-LO-3 (curiosity about new words and their meanings). Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-2, which is about locating a point of content.
'mukhya roop se' asks for the poem's overall subject - C-HIN2.1-LO-1, guessing the vishayvastu of a text. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-2, which is for hunting a specific detail.
Requires scanning the poem for every epithet applied to the land (punya-bhoomi, swarna-bhoomi, matribhoomi) - locating specific points, C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
What is shown waving (the rivers) is a stated detail. C-HIN2.1-LO-2, not LO-1's overall gist.
Who is calling (the koyal) - a specific point in the text. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Who kisses the sky (Himalaya) - stated in the opening line. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Where the birds chirp - a stated detail. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.

Match-the-following pairing words (malay pavan, sindhu, Himalaya, triveni, Ganga-Yamuna) with their meanings - a vocabulary exercise, C-HIN2.2-LO-3. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-2: the work is lexical, not about the poem's content.
Matches proper nouns (Raghupati, Shrikrishna, Sita, Gita, Gautam Buddha) with their glosses - word/reference meanings, C-HIN2.2-LO-3.

Matches poem lines to their paraphrases, which requires drawing the sense of each line - inferring and concluding, C-HIN2.1-LO-2. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-3, since whole lines rather than words are glossed.
The poet's purpose in writing is the poem's overall subject - C-HIN2.1-LO-1 rather than LO-2's specific point.
Buddha's message is a specific point the poem supplies. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.

'panktikaa aashay spasht keejiye' on a figurative line ('jagmag chhata nirali, pag-pag chhahar rahi hai') - attending to and appreciating how the poem's language works, C-HIN4.1-LO-1. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-2, which covers finding a point of content rather than appreciating the phrasing.
'kyon kaha gaya hai' needs the pupil to conclude from the poem why the land is called punya- and swarna-bhoomi - inferring, C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Names the epic characters and draws their importance - locating points and concluding from them, C-HIN2.1-LO-2. Rejected C-HIN3.1-LO-1, whose scope is local folk tales and folk songs, not the epics.
Why the land is called yuddha-bhoomi and buddha-bhoomi must be reasoned out; inference, C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Where the koyal lives - a stated detail. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
What refreshes body and mind (malay pavan) is stated. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Where the streams fall from - a stated detail. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
What Krishna played and taught is stated in the poem. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Whose fame Gautam raised - a specific point in the text. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.

The item is a word-meaning exercise: the key glosses 'lahar' and 'chhahar'. C-HIN2.2-LO-3. NB the stem is malformed - it prints only the quoted line, and the actual instruction has ended up inside the answer.
Where the splendour spreads requires reading the line closely and concluding. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Whose water waves (Ganga, Yamuna, Triveni) - a stated detail. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
The Himalaya's direction is concluded from the poem's imagery plus what the text states. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Who touches Bharat Mata's feet - a stated detail. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
'triveni shabd se aap kya samajhte hain' is a word-meaning question - C-HIN2.2-LO-3. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-2, since nothing of the poem's content is being located.

Explains the poetic phrase 'jagmag chhata nirali' - appreciating the poem's turn of language, C-HIN4.1-LO-1. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-3, which is for unfamiliar single words looked up in a dictionary, whereas this is a figurative phrase.
What sound the streams make (kal-kal) is stated in the poem. C-HIN2.1-LO-2. Rejected C-HIN1.1-LO-1, which is about presenting one's OWN experience of sounds orally.
Season and place of the koyal's song - stated details drawn together. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Where the cool fragrant winds come from is stated. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
What kind of country Bharat is (karma-pradhan) is the poem's own word. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
'kavita ke aadhaar par' - the great men are named in the text. C-HIN2.1-LO-2, not LO-1's overall gist.
Krishna's message in the Gita is a specific point. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
The path Buddha showed the world is stated. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.

Five-mark padyansh with five sub-questions - sustained close reading of a printed extract, which is C-HIN2.1-LO-2 (examining a text closely for specific points). Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1, which is skimming for the gist.
Second padyansh set, same skill: close reading for specific points. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Third padyansh set - close reading for specific points, C-HIN2.1-LO-2. NB the key is defective: items 2 and 3 are run together ('2.(ka) Sita (ga) karm karne ki') with question 3's number missing.
Asks the pupil to write their own view of a citizen's duties after reading the poem - expressing one's comment in writing, C-HIN4.2-LO-2. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-2: none of the answer is in the poem.
Kavyansh with four sub-questions on the first stanza - close reading for specific points, C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Kavyansh set on the rivers and their splendour - close reading, C-HIN2.1-LO-2.

Kavyansh set whose Q3 lists the poet's epithets (C-HIN2.1-LO-2, locating points) and whose Q4 asks what 'jharne' are (C-HIN2.2-LO-3, word meaning). Both cited because either alone would leave half the item unmapped.
Kavyansh set on the streams and birds - close reading for specific points. C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
Kavyansh set that includes an explicit paryayavachi question ('which word is NOT a synonym of pavan'), so C-HIN2.2-LO-3 alongside C-HIN2.1-LO-2 for the comprehension sub-questions.
Kavyansh set on the great men of the third stanza - close reading for specific points, C-HIN2.1-LO-2.
